(15 February 2014) | longest wins = | longest unbeaten = | longest winless = | longest losses = | highest attendance = | lowest attendance = | attendance = | average attendance = | prevseason = [[2013 Kenyan Premier League|2013]] | nextseason = [[2015 Kenyan Premier League|2015]] | extra information = | updated = 8 November 2014 }} The '''2014 Kenyan Premier League''' (known as the [[Tusker (African beer)|Tusker]] Premier League for sponsorship reasons) was the eleventh season of the [[Kenyan Premier League]] since it began in 2003. It was also the 51st season of top division [[football in Kenya]] since 1963. [[Gor Mahia F.C.|Gor Mahia]] won the league title for the second consecutive season, earning a place in the preliminary round of the [[2015 CAF Champions League]] while [[2014 FKF President's Cup]] champions [[Sofapaka F.C.|Sofapaka]] represented Kenya in the preliminary round of the [[2014 CAF Confederation Cup]]. The two teams faced each other at the [[2015 Kenyan Super Cup]]. A total of 16 teams competed for the league, with fourteen returning from the [[2013 Kenyan Premier League|2013 season]] and the [[2013 FKF Division One#Promotion play-offs|promotion play-off]] winners of [[FKF Division One]], which has since become the third tier of the [[Kenyan football league system]] after the introduction of the [[Kenyan National Super League|National Super League]] on 10 July 2013.{{cite web|title=New FKF soccer Structure to be implemented next year |url=http://www.michezoafrika.com/division-one/new-fkf-soccer-structure-to-be-implemented-next-year/13135 |date=10 July 2013 |author=Amos Abuga |publisher=MichezoAfrika.com |accessdate=11 July 2013}} ==Changes from last season== {{location map+ |Kenya |float=right |width=380 |caption=Locations of the 2014 Kenyan Premier League teams.|places= {{location map~ |Kenya |lat=-4.045006 |long=39.666154 |label=

Leopards]] was the season's first to be abandoned after fans of the latter invaded the pitch in the 85th minute, frustrated by their team's failure to get on the score sheet. At the time the match was called off, Thika United were leading 1–0.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/thika-leopards-match-called-off |title=Thika- Leopards match called off |date=11 May 2014 |author=Dennis Kituyi |publisher=Futaa.com |accessdate=11 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140512232022/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/thika-leopards-match-called-off |archive-date=12 May 2014 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}{{cite web|url=http://www.michezoafrika.com/kpl/thika-united-afc-leopards-match-abandoned/16336 |title=Thika United, AFC Leopards match abandoned |date=11 May 2014 |publisher=MichezoAfrika.com |accessdate=11 May 2014}} The KPL awarded Thika United a 2–0 victory, and A.F.C. Leopards were handed a fine of [[Kenyan shilling|KSh.]]500,000/= to be paid by 20 June 2014.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/afc-loses-thika-game-slapped-with-huge-fine |title=AFC loses Thika game, slapped with huge fine |date=21 May 2014 |author=Vincent Opiyo |publisher=Futaa.com |accessdate=22 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140522084714/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/afc-loses-thika-game-slapped-with-huge-fine |archive-date=22 May 2014 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }} On 26 October 2014, fans of [[Gor Mahia F.C.|Gor Mahia]] turned violent at the [[Kenyatta Stadium]] in Machakos after their team's 3–2 loss to [[Sofapaka F.C.|Sofapaka]]. Fans began throwing objects at the police after the match, and over an hour after the game both teams and a number of fans were still stranded at the stadium.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fans-police-engage-in-running-battles-after-sofa-a-gor-match |title=Fans, Police engage in running battles after Sofa – Gor match |date=26 October 2014 |author=Dan Ngulu |work=Futaa.com |accessdate=31 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141031204657/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fans-police-engage-in-running-battles-after-sofa-a-gor-match |archive-date=31 October 2014 |url-status=dead }} Following the match, [[Machakos County]] governor [[Alfred Mutua]] released a statement on behalf of the county government, banning Gor Mahia from the stadium "until further notice", and charging them [[Kenyan shilling|KSh.]]10 million/= as compensation for damage caused to public and private property.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/gor-mahia-banned |title=Gor Mahia banned |date=27 October 2014 |author=Kevin Teya |work=Futaa.com |accessdate=31 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141030074523/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/gor-mahia-banned |archive-date=30 October 2014 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web|url=http://www.michezoafrika.com/kpl/governor-mutua-bans-gor-mahia-wants-10m-as-compensation/17479 |title=Governor Mutua bans Gor Mahia, wants 10m as compensation |date=27 October 2014 |work=MichezoAfrika.com |accessdate=31 October 2014}} The [[Football Kenya Federation]] then fined the club KSh.500,000/= for the crowd trouble and ordered them to play their remaining league games behind closed doors, while Sofapaka were also fined KSh.300,000/= for failing to place sufficient security measures in the stadium as the host team.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/hooliganism-gor-mahia-sofapaka-fined-by-fkf |title=Hooliganism: Gor Mahia, Sofapaka fined by FKF |date=28 October 2014 |author=Wilson Mathu |work=Futaa.com |accessdate=31 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141031203214/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/hooliganism-gor-mahia-sofapaka-fined-by-fkf |archive-date=31 October 2014 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web|url=http://www.michezoafrika.com/kpl/gor-hit-big-as-fkf-slaps-fine/17482 |title=Gor hit big as FKF slaps fine |date=28 October 2014 |work=MichezoAfrika.com |accessdate=31 October 2014}} However, in response to the sanctions imposed on Gor Mahia by the Machakos County government, the club's secretary-general Chris Omondi announced that the club would not be "paying any cent to Mutua", questioning his authority to impose a ban on the club.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/gor-mahia-vows-not-to-pay-mutua-and-co |title=Gor Mahia vows not to pay
